ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A marble of radius 15 is rolled into a cone-shaped hole. It fits in perfectly. From the side the cone looks like an equilateral triangle. How deep is the hole?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image shows a cone-shaped hole in side/axial view, with the cone represented by a triangular cross-section and a marble represented by a circle/sphere fitting inside. The vertical arrow marks the depth from the rim/base line down to the cone tip. Reasoning: From the side, the cone is an equilateral triangle. Since the marble fits perfectly, its circular cross-section is the incircle of that equilateral triangle, tangent to the sides and the rim/base line. For an equilateral triangle, the inradius equals one-third of the altitude. The marble radius is 15, so the triangle altitude, which is the hole depth, is 3 × 15 = 45.

From the text, the cross-section triangle is equilateral and the marble radius is 15. Since the fitted marble corresponds to the incircle of the equilateral triangle, use the equilateral-triangle relation inradius = altitude/3. Thus depth = altitude = 3 × 15 = 45.
